headline: 284mm rain in 24h: Heavy rainfall paralyses Chittagong and hill districts
summary: Extreme rain has disrupted daily life, postponed HSC exams, and caused landslides that killed six people in Rangunia, Baghaichhari, and Cox's Bazar.
details: The Meteorological Department recorded 284 mm of rainfall in Chittagong between Tuesday morning and Wednesday morning, categorizing it as extremely heavy rainfall.
Active monsoon winds have disrupted normal life in the city, causing waterlogging in various areas and slowing down traffic and commerce.
Due to the severe weather, the Chittagong Education Board has postponed all HSC and equivalent examinations scheduled for today across all districts under its board.
The heavy rains have also triggered landslides. Six people were killed in Rangunia upazila of Chittagong, Baghaichhari in Rangamati, and Cox's Bazar yesterday.
Meteorologists warn that heavy to extremely heavy rainfall is likely to continue for at least the next two days in the Chittagong region.
The Chittagong City Corporation claims that most waterlogged areas cleared quickly because canals and drains were kept clean.
The current situation is driven by moist air from the Bay of Bengal creating frequent cloud formations during the mid-monsoon season.
caption:
284mm of rain in just 24 hours. Chittagong is underwater and the risk of landslides is critical.

The Meteorological Department recorded 284 mm of rainfall in Chittagong between Tuesday morning and Wednesday morning, categorizing it as extremely heavy rainfall.

Active monsoon winds have disrupted normal life in the city, causing waterlogging in various areas and slowing down traffic and commerce.

Due to the severe weather, the Chittagong Education Board has postponed all HSC and equivalent examinations scheduled for today across all districts under its board.

The heavy rains have also triggered landslides. Six people were killed in Rangunia upazila of Chittagong, Baghaichhari in Rangamati, and Cox's Bazar yesterday.

Meteorologists warn that heavy to extremely heavy rainfall is likely to continue for at least the next two days in the Chittagong region.

The Chittagong City Corporation claims that most waterlogged areas cleared quickly because canals and drains were kept clean.

The current situation is driven by moist air from the Bay of Bengal creating frequent cloud formations during the mid-monsoon season.

headline_marked: Major reshuffle: [[Government to appoint new Foreign Secretary]] and key envoys
headline: Major reshuffle: Government to appoint new Foreign Secretary and key envoys
summary: New appointments are set for the Foreign Secretary, Permanent Representatives to the UN in New York and Geneva, and High Commissioners to Delhi and London.
details: The government has decided on a major reshuffle within the Ministry of Foreign Affairs five months after the BNP government took office. This includes the appointment of a new Foreign Secretary and new representatives in New York, Delhi, London, and Geneva.

Salahuddin Noman Chowdhury, the current Permanent Representative to the UN in New York, is set to become the new Foreign Secretary. Meanwhile, current Foreign Secretary Asad Alam Siam will be appointed as the High Commissioner to India in Delhi.

Irene Khan, a renowned international human rights activist and former Secretary General of Amnesty International, is slated to be the Permanent Representative to the UN in New York. This appointment is noted as being based on political considerations.

Mohammad Abdul Muhit, the current Rector of the Foreign Service Academy, will be appointed as the High Commissioner to the UK in London. M Riaz Hamidullah, the current High Commissioner to India, will move to Geneva as the Permanent Representative.

Additionally, A K M Wahiduzzaman (Apelo), BNP's Information and Technology Secretary, is set to be appointed as Deputy Permanent Representative to the UN in New York. M Farhadul Islam will be appointed as the Ambassador to Mauritius.

The government has previously recalled four contract-based ambassadors appointed during the interim government's tenure. While three have returned, the High Commissioner to Maldives, Md. Nazmul Islam, has requested to remain at his post.
caption:
A major shake-up in Bangladesh's top diplomacy. New Foreign Secretary and key envoys for New York, Delhi, and London are being appointed.

The government has decided on a major reshuffle within the Ministry of Foreign Affairs five months after the BNP government took office. This includes the appointment of a new Foreign Secretary and new representatives in New York, Delhi, London, and Geneva.

Salahuddin Noman Chowdhury, the current Permanent Representative to the UN in New York, is set to become the new Foreign Secretary. Meanwhile, current Foreign Secretary Asad Alam Siam will be appointed as the High Commissioner to India in Delhi.

Irene Khan, a renowned international human rights activist and former Secretary General of Amnesty International, is slated to be the Permanent Representative to the UN in New York. This appointment is noted as being based on political considerations.

Mohammad Abdul Muhit, the current Rector of the Foreign Service Academy, will be appointed as the High Commissioner to the UK in London. M Riaz Hamidullah, the current High Commissioner to India, will move to Geneva as the Permanent Representative.

Additionally, A K M Wahiduzzaman (Apelo), BNP's Information and Technology Secretary, is set to be appointed as Deputy Permanent Representative to the UN in New York. M Farhadul Islam will be appointed as the Ambassador to Mauritius.

The government has previously recalled four contract-based ambassadors appointed during the interim government's tenure. While three have returned, the High Commissioner to Maldives, Md. Nazmul Islam, has requested to remain at his post.
